column1: # boru Language Specification: Predicate types (fnpred)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# fnpred is fnsig's mirror. `fn` takes input, output and body; each of the
# other two drops the slot it does not need:
#     fn      input  output  body     the whole function
#     fnsig   input  output           minus the BODY   → a function TYPE
#     fnpred  input          body     minus the OUTPUT → a predicate TYPE
# A predicate's output is not a choice — it is membership — so there is no
# output slot to write. Bound to a capitalised name, the result is a type
# every typed slot enforces.
# WHY IT EXISTS (NUR099). Without it the only route to an arbitrary
# predicate type is a capitalised `def` over a fn body, which makes the CASE
# of the name decide whether a body is a callable function or a membership
# test, and makes the parameter COUNT decide whether the binding is a
# predicate at all — an arity-keyed exception ADR-016 forbids. `fnpred` says
# it instead of inferring it.
# WHERE THE `is` ROWS ARE. `4 is Even` is the headline spelling, and it does
# not compile: a predicate type's body is a function value, and a function
# value reaching `is` is a Stage 3 compile failure — pre-existing, and identical for
# the capitalised-fn form this word replaces. Those rows therefore live in
# lang/spec/frontier/frontier-fnpred.tsv with a ledger entry, which is why
# no `is` row appears below. Every row here compiles; the typed-def and
# typed-param forms exercise the same membership through slots that do.
# §1  The pair form — fnpred <input> <body>
def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  typeof Even
column3: the node is parented at the INPUT type, so it inherits Integer's capabilities

column1: def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  def p:Even 4  p
column3: a typed def admits a member

column1: def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  def q:Even 5  q
column3: …and declines a non-member

column1: # §2  The spec-list form — a LIST input always selects it, exactly as with fn
def Even fnpred [[n:Integer] [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]]  def p:Even 4  p
column3: the spec-list form is the same type

column1: def Even fnpred [[n:Integer] [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]]  def q:Even 5  q
column3: …and declines the same values

column1: # §3  Both membership conventions — the body chooses
#     (a) return a Boolean
def Big fnpred n:Integer [n gt 10]  def p:Big 50  p
column3: Boolean convention: true means member

column1: def Big fnpred n:Integer [n gt 10]  def q:Big 5  q
column3: …and false means not

column1: #     (b) None-on-failure: the VALUE for a member, none for a non-member
def Positive fnpred n:Integer [if (n gt 0) [n] [None]]  def p:Positive 5  p
column3: None-on-failure: a non-none result means member

column1: def Positive fnpred n:Integer [if (n gt 0) [n] [None]]  def q:Positive 0  q
column3: …and none means not

column1: # §4  A predicate type is a TYPE: dispatch enforces it at parameters
def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  def f fn [[n:Even] [Integer] [n]]  f 4
column3: a parameter admits a member

column1: def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  def f fn [[n:Even] [Integer] [n]]  f 5
column3: …and dispatch declines a non-member

column1: # §5  The capitalised-fn form it replaces is refused at the declaration
#     (NUR099): a fn body is a type only through fnpred, so the case of a
#     name no longer decides whether a body is a function or a test.
def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  def p:Even 4  p
column3: fnpred…

column1: def Even fn n:Integer Boolean [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  def p:Even 4  p
column3: …and the legacy capitalised-fn spelling is refused at the declaration (NUR099): a fn body is a type only through fnpred

column1: def K fn [[a:Any b:Any][Any][a]] end  K 1 2
column3: the two-parameter combinator used to bind a type nothing could inhabit, silently — refused at the declaration

column1: def k fn [[a:Any b:Any][Any][a]] end  k 1 2
column3: …and its lower-case spelling is the callable function

column1: # §6  Negatives — the spec list takes PAIRS, not triples
#     (both are runtime-only shape errors: the checker cannot statically
#     flag a malformed spec list, so they carry an unflaggedPins entry.)
def E fnpred [[n:Integer]]
column3: an odd-length spec list: pairs, not triples

column1: def E fnpred [[n:Integer] [1] [2]]
column3: …and a triple is not a pair — that is `fn`

column1: #     A well-shaped pair whose INPUT is not a valid param spec fails in
#     construction, exactly as `fn`'s does — fnpred adds no new leniency.
def E fnpred [[n:NoSuchTypeXyz] [1]]
column3: an unknown param type is declined at construction

column1: # §7  `is` against a predicate type — the headline spelling for the
#     membership a fnpred declaration creates.
#     These lived in lang/spec/frontier/frontier-fnpred.tsv until 2026-08-28,
#     ledgered as `function value reaches is (Stage 3)`. The compile failure was
#     never about `is`: a predicate NODE is a bare type literal that rides as
#     data, and the body runs through the callback seam, not the tape. What
#     blocked them was that the seam's nested arm declined every detached
#     unit, so the body interpreted inside the handler — admitting the rows
#     would have hidden an island rather than removed one. With foreign units
#     hostable (eng/go/vm_foreign_unit.go) the body runs on the VM, so the
#     rows compile AND stay honest; the interp-entry census is what keeps
#     that claim checkable.
def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  4 is Even
column3: an even Integer is a member

column1: def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  5 is Even
column3: an odd one is not

column1: def Even fnpred [[n:Integer] [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]]  4 is Even
column3: the spec-list form is the same type

column1: def Even fnpred [[n:Integer] [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]]  5 is Even
column3: …and declines the same values

column1: def Big fnpred n:Integer [n gt 10]  50 is Big
column3: Boolean convention: true means member

column1: def Big fnpred n:Integer [n gt 10]  5 is Big
column3: …and false means not

column1: def Positive fnpred n:Integer [if (n gt 0) [n] [None]]  5 is Positive
column3: None-on-failure: a non-none result means member

column1: def Positive fnpred n:Integer [if (n gt 0) [n] [None]]  0 is Positive
column3: …and none means not

column1: #     The input-type gate rejects before the body runs, so a predicate over
#     Integer never sees a String — and the TYPE itself is not an inhabitant
#     question: a bare node passes the gate as the type it is.
def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  "x" is Even
column3: the input-type gate rejects without running the body

column1: def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  Even is Even
column3: a type literal is the type itself, not an inhabitant

column1: # TWO REFERENCES TO ONE PREDICATE ARE THE SAME TYPE (NUR157, closed 2026-09-25):
# a `[:Pos]` pattern unifies with a `[:Pos]` pattern under a registry as it
# does without one; a different predicate still fails, membership is unchanged.
def Pos fnpred n:Integer [n gt 0] [:Pos] [:Pos] unify
column3: the same predicate's typed-list patterns unify as the type (NUR157)

column1: def Pos fnpred n:Integer [n gt 0] def Neg fnpred n:Integer [n lt 0] [:Neg] [:Pos] unify
column3: …and two different predicates do not

column1: def Pos fnpred n:Integer [n gt 0] [1 -2] [:Pos] unify
column3: membership is unchanged

column1: # §8  Membership is a ONE-VALUE APPLICATION (NUR100, closed 2026-09-26):
#     the candidate is matched against the predicate's signatures by the one
#     matcher every call takes, and the signature that takes it runs. No
#     parameter COUNT admits or refuses a function as a predicate — a
#     signature that cannot take one value is simply never the one selected,
#     as for any call — and the WHOLE overload set is consulted, first match
#     first, where only the first overload used to be read.
def P fnpred [[n:Integer] [n gt 0] [s:String] [(size s) gt 0]]  def v:P "ab"  v
column3: a later overload takes a value the first cannot — the whole set is consulted

column1: def P fnpred [[n:Integer] [n gt 0] [s:String] [(size s) gt 0]]  def v:P ""  v
column3: …and its body still decides membership

column1: def P fnpred [[n:Integer] [n gt 0] [s:String] [(size s) gt 0]]  def f fn [[q:P] [Any] [q]]  f "ab"
column3: a typed parameter consults the same overloads

column1: def P fnpred [[n:Integer] [n gt 0] [s:String] [(size s) gt 0]]  def f fn [[q:P] [Any] [q]]  f 0
column3: …and declines what every overload declines

column1: def P fnpred [[n:Integer] [n gt 0] [s:String] [(size s) gt 0]]  "ab" is P
column3: `is` asks the same question

column1: def P fnpred [[n:Integer] [n gt 0] [s:String] [(size s) gt 0]]  "" is P
column3: …with the same answer

column1: def K fnpred [[a:Any b:Any] [a]]  def v:K 5  v
column3: no signature takes ONE value, so no value is a member — the use answers membership, never an arity error

column1: def K fnpred [[a:Any b:Any] [a]]  4 is K
column3: …and `is` agrees

column1: def Z fnpred [[0] [true]]  0 is Z
column3: a value PATTERN selects as it does for any call

column1: def Z fnpred [[0] [true]]  1 is Z
column3: …and a value it does not match is not a member, with no body run

column1: #     An UNNAMED input the body leaves beneath its verdict is call-scoped data
#     the seam discards on both lanes, exactly as a call's frame does (NUR223).
def Z fnpred [[Integer] [dup 0 eq]]  0 is Z
column3: the verdict is the top of the residual; the unconsumed input is discarded

column1: def Z fnpred [[Integer] [dup 0 eq]]  1 is Z
column3: …and a false verdict stays false
